editorial:
Ever feel like the only person who sees the truth while everyone else thinks you are crazy? That is exactly where you find Neil Stuart, a tutor in a quiet New England town who is tired of being the local joke. He knows a scary monster called the Riverbeast is hiding in the water, and he is determined to prove it. You will love the campy, old-school vibe here because it feels like those goofy monster movies from the 1950s. Neil team up with his pretty student, some fellow tutors, and a former pro athlete to stop the creature before it eats the whole town. It is a wild ride that does not take itself too seriously.

The acting is charmingly over-the-top, which adds to the comedy, though the monster effects are a bit cheesy. The pacing stays quick, so you will not get bored, even if some of the plot twists are easy to guess. If you love movies that are more about having a laugh than being truly scared, you should definitely give this a go. It is best watched with a bowl of popcorn and some friends who enjoy B-movies.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, Neil and his crew lure the Riverbeast into a trap using a mix of bravery and luck. They use a huge electric shock to stun the creature, allowing them to finally kill it for good. The town finally realizes Neil was right all along, and he goes from being the local laughingstock to a hometown hero. Everyone celebrates their survival, and Neil finally gets the respect he deserved from the start.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cheesy monster movies and retro vibes.
